title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed page numbered 41, from a French typescript on quasi-functions and heights on abelian varieties. Its notation and style match A. Néron's theory: quasi-fonctions, Q*(V), B*(V), M_K̄ the set of absolute values, D_l and D_a for divisors linearly or algebraically equivalent to 0, and Z_o(A) for 0-cycles of degree 0. This is very likely a preprint of Néron, 'Quasi-fonctions et hauteurs sur les variétés abéliennes', Ann. of Math. 82 (1965). It was filed in the 1965-69 crystals folder, with archive sheet number 33 handwritten. The neighbouring pages are genuinely Grothendieck, on divided powers.

Modern content:

(1) Notation for 0-cycles. For a class q in Q*(A), a class of quasi-functions (functions on A(K̄)×M_K̄ that are locally log-bounded and attached to divisors), and a 0-cycle a = Σ m_i(a_i), set q_a = Π q_{a_i}^{m_i}, where q_u is the translate by u. Then div(q_a) = (div q)_a. For a of degree 0, the real number q_o(a,v) = Σ m_i log|r(a_i)|_v-type value is independent of the representative, because the ambiguous constants cancel. Néron writes it q(a,v).

(2) Principal quasi-functions. For X a divisor linearly equivalent to 0 and f with div f = X, the class of the principal quasi-function f̃ depends only on X. Call it f(X).

(3) The map ξ_o. Q*_l(A) and Q*_a(A) are the classes whose divisor is linearly (resp. algebraically) equivalent to 0. For q in Q*_l(A), set ξ_o(q) = f(div q)·q^{-1}. It has divisor 0, so it lies in B*(A), the classes of bounded quasi-functions. This gives a homomorphism Q*_l(A) → B*(A) commuting with translations.

(4) Relation (15), a reciprocity/symmetry statement. For degree-0 cycles a, b with X_a and X_{b^-} linearly equivalent to 0:
 ξ_o(q_a)(b,v) = ξ_o(q_{b^-})(a^-,v) = ξ_o(q^-_b)(a,v).
This is the local, Weil-reciprocity-type symmetry underlying the Néron local pairing ⟨D, a⟩_v between degree-0 divisors and 0-cycles, and hence the bilinearity and symmetry of the canonical height.

(5) Start of the proof. Choose f with div f = X_a and r representing q. Then ξ_o(q_a)(b,v) = (f̃ r_a^{-1})(b,v) = (f̃ r_a^{-1})_{b^-}(0,v), i.e. a translation reduces evaluation at b to evaluation at the origin.
errors: Typo in the typescript: 'pour a, b Z_o(A)' is missing '∈'.
The parenthetical '(i.e. q_a et q_b ∈ Q*_l(A))' should read q_a and q_{b^-} to match X_{b^-} ~ 0. In the image the subscripts appear hand-altered.
'q_a = ∏_i m_i q_{a_i}' means the multiplicatively written product with exponents m_i. This is notation, not an error. No mathematical errors are visible in what is stated.

ideas.what: Quasi-functions on a variety over a field with absolute values, modulo bounded ones (Q*, B*); values on degree-0 cycles independent of normalization
ideas.modern_name: Néron functions / local height functions (Weil functions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Néron (1965), building on Weil's distributions/Weil functions
ideas.where_published: Néron, Ann. of Math. 82 (1965); this page appears to be Néron's own typescript

ideas.what: Homomorphism ξ_o: Q*_l(A) → B*(A), q ↦ f(div q)·q^{-1}, commuting with translations
ideas.modern_name: Comparison between a Néron function of a principal divisor and log|f|_v; translation-invariant correction term
Reciprocity/symmetry of the Néron local height pairing (generalized Weil reciprocity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Néron; later reinterpreted via biextensions by Grothendieck (SGA 7 VII–VIII), Moret-Bailly, Zarhin
ideas.where_published: Néron 1965; the biextension viewpoint is in SGA 7 and later literature

missed.claim: This sheet is a typescript page by Néron (on quasi-functions and heights), not Grothendieck's notes, though it is filed in the crystals/de Rham folder. It documents that Grothendieck had Néron's height theory at hand in the period when he developed biextensions, which are known to reinterpret Néron's local pairings. This is archival context only, not a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: Pour q ∈ Q*_l(A), nous poserons ξ_o(q) = f(div(q)) q^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Cataloguing: the folder description should note a foreign typescript. Historically, it is minor evidence for the Néron-pairing motivation behind SGA 7 biextensions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed excerpt of Néron's published theory of quasi-functions and local heights. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics, and the only oddity is its misfiling in the crystals folder.
